root_cause.text: In `net/phonet/socket.c`, `pn_socket_autobind()` incorrectly treated any `-EINVAL` from `pn_socket_bind()` as evidence that the socket was already bound, then `BUG_ON()`ed if `pn_port()` was still zero; but `pn_socket_bind()` can also return `-EINVAL` for an unbound socket when `sk->sk_state != TCP_CLOSE`, making the `BUG_ON()` reachable from a user-triggerable send path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explains that `pn_socket_bind()` “also returns -EINVAL when sk->sk_state is not TCP_CLOSE, even when the socket has never been bound and pn_port() is still 0,” and changes `pn_socket_autobind()` from `BUG_ON(!pn_port(pn_sk(sock->sk)->sobject));` to returning `err` when `err != -EINVAL || unlikely(!pn_port(...))`, proving the crash came from assuming `-EINVAL` always meant “already bound.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pn_socket_autobind() to avoid crashing on ambiguous -EINVAL returns by only treating them as already-bound when a port is actually assigned.
intent_record.what: In pn_socket_autobind(), the existing check `if (err != -EINVAL)` was changed to `if (err != -EINVAL || unlikely(!pn_port(pn_sk(sock->sk)->sobject)))`, and the `BUG_ON(!pn_port(pn_sk(sock->sk)->sobject));` line was removed. A new comment was added explaining that `pn_socket_bind()` can return `-EINVAL` both for an already-bound socket and for `sk_state != TCP_CLOSE` without a prior bind.
intent_record.how: The function no longer treats every `-EINVAL` from `pn_socket_bind()` as evidence that the socket was already bound. If `-EINVAL` is returned but the port is still zero, the error is now propagated instead of triggering a kernel BUG, preventing a crash in cases where bind fails for reasons other than prior autobind state.

grouping_result.intent: Fix pn_socket_autobind() to avoid crashing on ambiguous -EINVAL returns by only treating them as already-bound when a port is actually assigned.

The fix limits that assumption to cases where a port is actually assigned, which matches the vulnerability.
